Induce

/in-DOOS/ - rhymes with juice · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Induce means to bring something about or cause it to begin.

A darkened room and a cool pillow will often induce the sleep that no amount of counting could.

Worked Example

Faraday's trick still opens half the physics textbooks in print: a coil of wire, a bar magnet, and a needle that leaps the moment the magnet moves. The wire touches nothing. The magnet hands it nothing you can point to. Yet slide the bar through the coil and a current flows that was not there a heartbeat before — called into being by the motion alone.

Induce is the exact word — physicists say the magnet induces the current — because to induce is to bring something about or cause it to begin. The current was not hiding in the wire waiting to be released; the conditions summoned it. Trigger fires something already primed and waiting; induce takes credit for the whole beginning.

How Induce Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

bring on

bring on: the everyday phrase — bring on sleep, bring on rain

prompt

prompt: nudges a thing into starting; induce takes fuller credit for the beginning

Antonyms

avert

avert: turns the thing aside before it can begin

block

block: the wall's answer — nothing begins because nothing gets through

How Strong Is It? — nudge → induce → force

nudge vs. induce

nudge vs. induce: A nudge tilts the odds and no more — the thing may still never happen.

force vs. induce

force vs. induce: Force goes further than induce — an induced process was coaxed from conditions that were ready; a forced one is dragged out whether the conditions were ready or not.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of induce.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — in-

Prefix — in-: in, toward

Root — duc

Root — duc: to lead (Latin ducere)

Put it together

Put it together: In- (toward) + duc (to lead) = to lead into being. Latin ducere is the great leading root — dukes lead armies, conductors lead orchestras — and inducere aims the leading at a beginning: coax the conditions into line, and the effect follows as if led by the hand.

Use the root in a new word: aqueduct

Use the root in a new word: aqueduct: An aqueduct literally leads water — aqua + duct — across whole valleys to the city's fountains.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral / scientific

Induce is the lab's and the clinic's verb — doctors induce labor, chemists induce reactions, a warm bath induces drowsiness. It judges nothing and needs no villain, which sets it apart in this unit: instigate and incite need someone working on people; induce works just as happily on sleep, currents, and rain. For an instantaneous set-off, trigger is the sharper word.
